summary: IDC delivers Nabd's trust layer for patients and clinicians: Phase 0 PHI read gates, tenant processing consent with versioned per-facility notices, the caregiver/guardian model, OTP secure links, ABDM M1-M3, data-subject rights with retention and legal hold, the Cedar policy engine for intra-hospital access and break-glass, and in Phase 3 the global Person/Practitioner identity plane with one-login facility switching and consented, time-boxed cross-facility sharing through the Exchange (never by widening RLS). stories.title: Clinical reads stop returning a patient who withdrew consent or is outside the doctor's own-patients scope
stories.story: As a patient I want my clinical record to disappear from every clinical screen once I withdraw processing consent, and to be visible only to the doctors allowed to see it, so that my choice and the clinic's access rules are enforced by the server and not by the UI.
stories.context: Today the consent-withdrawal gate (CONSENT_GATE), the own-patients scope (SCOPE_GATE) and the dual-verification gate exist only in PatientRepository on /v1/patients/**. Every /v1/clinical/** controller (notes, prescriptions, vitals, allergies, conditions, timeline, encounter list, documents, pregnancy status, dental, vaccines) returns full history for any patient id in the tenant (doc 02 finding 6, MF-17). This story ports the gates into the clinical SQL itself through one shared ClinicalReadScope fragment so a missing gate fails a test, and applies staff.field_grants on every clinical DTO, not just in one place. A withdrawn or out-of-scope patient returns 404 (not 403) so that existence is not leaked. This is the Phase 0 bridge; IDC-027 later replaces the SQL gates with the Cedar PEP. Writes are out of scope (they already require an open encounter). Exit-gate item for Sprint 2.

Given a staff member whose field_grants exclude 'diagnosis', when they read notes, timeline or encounter list, then the diagnosis fields are null in every DTO (not only in the timeline)
Given the clinical read-scope test suite, when a new GET endpoint is added under /v1/clinical/** without the ClinicalReadScope fragment, then the architecture test fails the build
